title: The rewrite that is never worth it, and the two cases where it is

videos.script: Sooner or later somebody proposes it. The old system is a mess, so throw it away and write it again, properly this time. {{proposal}} At Coreto the proposal is to rewrite the reservation module from scratch. Six engineers, eighteen months, a clean start. It sounds brave, and it is usually the most expensive way to fail. {{core}} This lesson starts with why. The old code holds years of fixes nobody wrote down. The second version of a system tends to carry everything its designers held back the first time. And the old system does not stand still while the new one catches up. {{why}} Then the two cases where a rewrite is the right call. The system is small enough to rewrite within a quarter, behind a switch you can flip back. Or the ground under it is going away and there is no path one piece at a time. {{cases}} Last, the sum. You put the proposal's own numbers in your spreadsheet, and then the same numbers with an overrun. {{sum}}
